reason: The hypothesis cites no prior evidence, and all key premises—from the formation of short-range order by annealing to its effect on dislocation motion and strength—are specific claims requiring experimental support that is not provided.
premises: Thermal annealing can induce short-range chemical order in multi-component concentrated alloys.
Short-range order generates local lattice distortions.
These lattice distortions act as obstacles that impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion increases yield strength and alters deformation behavior.
The effect is measurable in single-phase alloys with atomic size mismatch under quasi-static loading.
